title: Five days to move money
where: ESM, Kirchberg — Lending Operations, fourth floor

lines.text: Rain over the Kirchberg plateau, the kind that hangs rather than falls. Not light yet. The fourth floor has been switched on since half past six.
lines.plain: It is raining in Kirchberg. It is still dark outside. The lights on the fourth floor have been on since 06:30.

lines.text: Grace Hopper is standing at a desk that is not hers, reading over Marie Curie's shoulder. Nobody has told you why you were asked to come up.
lines.plain: Grace Hopper stands behind Marie Curie and reads her screen. Nobody told you why you were asked to come to this floor.

lines.text: You are the Project Support Office. Sit there. Ten minutes, then tell me whether I am exaggerating.
lines.plain: You work in the Project Support Office. Sit here. Watch for ten minutes. Then tell me if I am making this sound worse than it is.
ref: The Project Support Office (PSO) ... is an optional structure that can provide services to project teams such as the application of the methodology and use of the artefacts, information systems, governance, logistics and various support.

lines.text: Exaggerating about what?
lines.plain: About what?

lines.text: That is what the ten minutes are for.
lines.plain: That is what the ten minutes are for.

lines.text: Disbursement instruction. Third tranche, two hundred and fifty million. Value date Monday.
lines.plain: This is a disbursement instruction. It is the third part of a loan. The amount is 250 million euro. The money must be in the country's account on Monday.
g: disbursement
paying out an agreed part of a loan to the borrower on a fixed date
value date
the day the money must actually sit in the receiving account

lines.text: It exists here, in LOS. Complete. Checked. Signed. Now watch.
lines.plain: The instruction is already in LOS, our lending system. It is complete, checked and signed. Now watch what I do next.

lines.text: She opens the treasury system beside it and starts typing. Not fast. Field, glance, field.
lines.plain: She opens the treasury system next to it and types the same information again. She types slowly. One field, then a look at the first screen, then the next field.

lines.text: You are typing it again.
lines.plain: You are typing the same information a second time.

lines.text: Twenty-two fields. Then a third time, into the payment gateway. Then the second officer reads all three against each other before the four o'clock cut-off.
lines.plain: Twenty-two fields. Then I type them a third time, into the payment gateway. Then a second officer compares all three versions before the 16:00 deadline.

lines.text: And if he disagrees with you?
lines.plain: What happens if he does not agree with you?

lines.text: Then one of us is wrong and we find out which. That is the control. A person. Reading.
lines.plain: Then one of us made a mistake and we find out who. That check is the control. It is one person reading the work of another. We call it four eyes.
g: four-eyes principle
a rule that a second person must check and approve work before it takes effect

lines.text: About fourteen hundred fields a quarter. We counted them. Audit made us count them.
lines.plain: About 1,400 fields every three months are typed again by hand. We counted them because the internal auditors asked us to.
ref: Identify measurable criteria that will be used to determine the success of the project.

lines.text: Two findings, I heard.
lines.plain: I heard the auditors raised two findings.

lines.text: Segregation of duties is one. The trail is two. You can see what LOS holds this morning. You cannot always see who changed it, or when.
lines.plain: Yes. The first finding is about who is allowed to do which step. The second is about the record of changes. You can see what LOS contains today. You cannot always see who changed it, or when.

lines.text: LOS was written in the EFSF era and extended every year since. Fourteen years. Three people in the building can read the parts that matter, and two of them are contractors.
lines.plain: LOS was built in the EFSF period, fourteen years ago, and changed every year since. Only three people here can read its most important parts. Two of them are contractors.
g: EFSF
European Financial Stability Facility, the temporary euro area rescue fund that the ESM replaced

lines.text: Instruction to value date. How long?
lines.plain: How many days pass between the instruction and the day the money arrives?

lines.text: Five working days when nothing surprises us. Reconciliation afterwards, three more.
lines.plain: Five working days if nothing goes wrong. After the payment, reconciliation takes three more days.
g: reconciliation
checking that the records of two systems match, and explaining every difference
ref: the document describes the impact the project is expected to bring and summarises the success criteria against which it will be evaluated

lines.text: And a new instrument means new code. The last one took nine months from decision to first disbursement.
lines.plain: And a new lending product means new software. The last one took nine months from the decision to the first payment.

lines.text: If the Treaty reform finishes ratifying, the common backstop arrives as a new instrument.
lines.plain: If the Treaty reform is approved by all member states, the common backstop will arrive as a new lending product.

lines.text: Italy has not ratified, so it is planned rather than live and everybody is comfortable. The day it stops being planned we will have weeks and we will need nine months.
lines.plain: Italy has not approved the reform yet. So the backstop is only planned, not real, and nobody worries. On the day it becomes real we will have a few weeks, and we will need nine months.

lines.text: Sorry. Cut-off.
lines.plain: Excuse me. I have to finish before the deadline.

lines.text: So what are you asking me for?
lines.plain: What do you want from me?

lines.text: Nothing yet. I have half an hour of Florence tomorrow, and I wanted to be able to say I had shown this to somebody who does projects for a living.
lines.plain: Nothing yet. I have thirty minutes with Florence Nightingale tomorrow. I wanted to be able to say that I showed this to a project professional.
ref: This is an informal meeting, usually between the project initiator and the Project Owner (PO), and others who could potentially contribute to the creation of the Initiating Phase documents.

lines.text: Show her the printout. She signs the exceptions every month. She has never once watched anybody type them.
lines.plain: Show her the paper. She signs the exception reports every month. She has never watched anyone type the payment by hand.

lines.text: No project. No budget, no charter, no name, no team. A floor of people working around a problem, and a printout with twenty-two boxes on it.
lines.plain: There is no project yet. No money, no charter, no name, no team. There is only a floor of people working around a problem, and a paper with twenty-two boxes on it.
ref: It begins with the identification of a need, problem or opportunity, and ends with the establishment of the plans and processes needed to take the project forward.

you.o: Nothing yet. A Project Manager employed in the Project Support Office, not assigned to this or any project.
you.k: Knows LOS is old and slow. Has now seen the manual re-keying once, with numbers attached.
you.w: Wants to know why the fourth floor asked for someone from the Project Support Office.
you.f: Afraid of being used as decoration in somebody else's internal argument.

hopper.o: Nothing formally. Senior Loan Operations Officer, and the person who will raise the request.
hopper.k: Knows the field counts and both audit findings. Has no idea what a replacement costs.
hopper.w: Wants a witness she can quote to Nightingale tomorrow afternoon.
hopper.f: Afraid the thirty-minute slot produces sympathy and no decision.

curie.o: Performs the disbursement by hand today. Loan Administration Officer in Lending Operations.
curie.k: Knows every manual step because she carries them out and signs for them.
curie.w: Wants Monday's value date met before the four o'clock cut-off.
curie.f: Afraid a new system quietly removes the second pair of eyes.

note: Guide check: the Initiating Phase begins with the identification of a need, problem or opportunity (p.31). Nothing here is a PM² project yet. No Project Initiation Request exists, so formally there is no Project Owner, no Solution Provider and no assigned Project Manager, and there is no RASCI row to sit in. You are a Project Manager employed in the Project Support Office, not the Project Manager of anything. Approver: none, because there is nothing to approve. Page 31.
notePlain: Rule: a PM² project starts when someone identifies a need, a problem or an opportunity (page 31). Here that has happened, but nothing is written down. So there is no project yet: no Project Owner, no Solution Provider, no Project Manager. Nobody approves anything in this scene, because there is nothing to approve. You work in the Project Support Office. That is a support service, not a role on this project.

title: Thirty minutes in B4-12
where: ESM, Kirchberg — meeting room B4-12, the one with the video kit nobody trusts

lines.text: B4-12 seats eight and has one screen that gives everybody a green cast. Leonardo da Vinci is two floors down and joins by video anyway, because the room he wanted was taken.
lines.plain: Room B4-12 has eight seats and one screen that makes everyone look green. Leonardo da Vinci works two floors below. He joins by video because the room he wanted was booked.

lines.text: Thirty minutes. Funding plan at three, and I am not moving it.
lines.plain: You have thirty minutes. I have a funding meeting at 15:00 and I will not move it.

lines.text: Five working days to a value date. Three more to reconcile. Fourteen hundred fields a quarter, re-keyed by hand. Two audit findings, both sitting on LOS.
lines.plain: It takes five working days to pay money out, and three more days to check the records. Every three months staff type 1,400 fields again by hand. There are two open audit findings, both about LOS.

lines.text: I have known that for two years.
lines.plain: I have known all of that for two years.

lines.text: Leonardo's audio arrives about half a second after his mouth.
lines.plain: On the video screen, Leonardo's sound arrives about half a second after his lips move.

lines.text: Four.
lines.plain: Four years.

lines.text: What?
lines.plain: Sorry, what?

lines.text: IT has known for four. Fourteen years old, and every new instrument is bespoke code.
lines.plain: The IT division has known for four years. The system is fourteen years old, and every new lending product needs software written specially for it.

lines.text: Am I minuting this?
lines.plain: Should I write official minutes of this meeting?

lines.text: There is nothing to minute. Write it in your own book.
lines.plain: There is nothing official to record yet. Just take notes for yourself.
ref: This is an informal meeting, usually between the project initiator and the Project Owner (PO), and others who could potentially contribute to the creation of the Initiating Phase documents.

lines.text: So we buy something. There are three vendors in this market and I could name all three from memory.
lines.plain: So we should buy a product. Three companies sell this kind of system, and I can name all three without looking.

lines.text: You could name them. Neither of us could yet say what we would be buying.
lines.plain: You can name them. But neither you nor I can yet say what exactly we would be buying.

lines.text: One instruction, entered once. Loan agreement to disbursement to repayment schedule, with nobody retyping it. Instruments configured, not coded. Reconciliation the same day. The word for it is straight-through processing.
lines.plain: One instruction, typed once. It travels from the loan agreement to the payment to the repayment schedule, and nobody types it again. New lending products are set up by configuration, not by new software. Records are checked the same day. The name for this is straight-through processing.
g: straight-through processing
data passes from one system to the next automatically, with nobody typing it again
payment gateway
the system that sends the payment message to the banks that move the money

lines.text: Cost.
lines.plain: What does it cost?

lines.text: Eight and a half. Give or take two.
lines.plain: About eight and a half million euro. The real figure could be two million higher or lower.

lines.text: Two million.
lines.plain: Two million euro either way.

lines.text: I would want six weeks with the payment gateway before I said anything firmer. It drops the value date if the instruction arrives after sixteen hundred, and nobody has ever written down why.
lines.plain: I would need six weeks looking at the payment gateway before I gave you a firmer number. If an instruction arrives after 16:00, the gateway loses the value date, and nobody ever wrote down the reason.
ref: The Project Initiation Request contains basic information about the estimated effort and cost of undertaking the project as well as the timeframe for its completion and the type of delivery.

lines.text: Has the house done anything like this before?
lines.plain: Has this organisation done a project like this before?

lines.text: Collateral register replacement, three years ago. I can pull the Project-End Report. Two pages of lessons learned. One page is entirely about business experts promised part-time who delivered part of part-time.
lines.plain: Yes. We replaced the collateral register three years ago. I can find the Project-End Report. It has two pages of lessons learned. One whole page is about business experts who were promised part-time and gave much less than that.
ref: Documentation and lessons learned from previous similar projects can also be used as input to this meeting.

lines.text: That one will happen to us. Print it.
lines.plain: That problem will happen to us too. Please print the report.

lines.text: Twelve minutes.
lines.plain: You have twelve minutes left.

lines.text: Florence. Own this. Not supportive in corridors. Own it.
lines.plain: Florence, I need you to own this project. Not just to say kind things about it in the corridor. Own it.

lines.text: Lending Operations pays for it, is blamed for it, and either gets the benefit or does not. Yes. I own it.
lines.plain: My division pays for it. My division is blamed if it fails. My division gets the benefit, or gets nothing. Yes. I own it.
g: Project Owner
the client of the project, accountable for its success and for the benefits it should bring
ref: As the key Directing Layer role from the requestor side, the Project Owner (PO) is accountable for the overall project's success, and later becomes the owner of the project's outputs (product or service).

lines.text: Then IT provides. Whatever this turns out to be, my division builds it and I answer for what comes out of it.
lines.plain: Then the IT division will provide the solution. Whatever we decide to build, my division builds it, and I answer for the result.
g: Solution Provider
the manager whose unit produces the project's deliverables and answers for them
ref: Assumes overall accountability for the project deliverables and services requested by the Project Owner (PO).

lines.text: Two names on a whiteboard with no document underneath them. Gantt writes them down anyway, in a notebook that is not an artefact of anything.
lines.plain: Two names are now on the whiteboard, but no document exists under them. Gantt writes them in his own notebook, which is not an official project document.
ref: The main beneficiary of the project's outputs usually nominates a Project Owner (PO). ... The organisational unit that will carry out the project work nominates a Solution Provider (SP).

lines.text: You do this professionally, apparently. What happens next?
lines.plain: I am told this is your profession. What is the next step?

choice.prompt: Florence has eight minutes left. What is the next step?
choice.promptPlain: Florence has eight minutes left. What do you tell her the next step is?

options.t: One page. A Project Initiation Request, asking only for permission to write a Business Case.
options.tPlain: Write one page: a Project Initiation Request. It asks only for permission to write a Business Case.

reply.text: One page I can read before three o'clock. Draft it over the weekend and I will look at it Monday.
reply.plain: One page that I can read before 15:00. Write it this weekend and I will read it on Monday.

options.why: The Initiating Meeting is informal, between the initiator and the Project Owner plus anyone who can contribute, and its result is a decision to move forward with the creation of the Project Initiation Request (p.31). That request captures the situation and the desired outcomes, with high-level effort, cost, timeframe and type of delivery (p.32). Approving it authorises work on a more elaborate Business Case, and nothing else.
options.whyPlain: This meeting is informal. Its only job is to agree the next step, and the next step is a Project Initiation Request (page 31). That request describes the problem and the wanted result, plus rough effort, cost, time and how the work will be delivered (page 32). Approving it only allows the team to write a Business Case. It approves nothing else.
ref: The result of this meeting is a better understanding of the context of the (future) project, as well as a decision to move forward with the creation of the Project Initiation Request.

options.t: Book the Corporate Investment Board for Monday and ask Lorenzo de' Medici for eight and a half million.
options.tPlain: Ask for a slot at the Corporate Investment Board on Monday, and ask Lorenzo de' Medici for eight and a half million euro.

reply.text: With what? A photograph of a whiteboard. He would ask what he is buying and I would have nothing at all to hand him.
reply.plain: With what document? A photo of a whiteboard. He would ask what he is paying for, and I would have nothing to give him.

options.why: The governance body is the right one but the sequence is wrong. The Project Initiation Request is the vehicle that goes to the approver, informally to the Project Owner or formally to an Appropriate Governance Body (p.32). Arriving at a portfolio body with no request and no Business Case asks it to fund something nobody has yet described in writing.
options.whyPlain: The committee is correct, but the order is wrong. The document that goes to an approver is the Project Initiation Request (page 32). Without it, and without a Business Case, you are asking a senior committee to pay for something that nobody has written down.
ref: Depending on the project, the Project Owner (PO) or a higher-level Appropriate Governance Body (AGB) can accept the Project Initiation Request and authorise work on a more elaborate Business Case.

options.t: Give me six weeks and I will bring you a fully costed Business Case with options.
options.tPlain: Ask for six weeks, then bring back a complete Business Case with costed options.

reply.text: Six weeks of whose time, on whose authority? Nothing has been approved. You would be spending a budget that does not exist.
reply.plain: Six weeks of whose working time, approved by whom? Nothing has been approved yet. You would be spending money that has not been given to you.

options.why: The Business Case comes second and its input is the Project Initiation Request (p.34). It is also not the Project Manager's document: the Business Manager is Responsible and the Project Owner Accountable, with the PM only Supporting, and the PM is typically not even assigned until after the Business Case is approved (pp.32, 35).
options.whyPlain: The Business Case comes after the Project Initiation Request, and uses it as input (page 34). It is also not your document. The Business Manager writes it, the Project Owner is accountable for it, and the Project Manager only helps. A Project Manager is usually assigned only after it is approved (pages 32 and 35).
ref: Inputs • Project Initiation Request

options.t: Minute this as the project kick-off, open the Risk Log and run a risk workshop next week.
options.tPlain: Record this meeting as the official project start, open the Risk Log, and hold a risk workshop next week.

reply.text: Kick-off for what? There is no charter to kick off and no team to invite.
reply.plain: The start of what? There is no charter yet, and there is no team to invite.

options.why: The Initiating Meeting is informal by design (p.31). The Planning Kick-off Meeting is a different, formal meeting that opens the Planning Phase after the RfP gate (p.40). The Risk, Issue and Decision Logs are set up during Initiating, but they attach to a project that has at least been requested (p.31).
options.whyPlain: This meeting is meant to be informal (page 31). The Planning Kick-off Meeting is a different, formal meeting that starts the Planning Phase, after the first gate (page 40). The Risk, Issue and Decision Logs are opened during Initiating, but only for a project that has been requested (page 31).
ref: Some of the Project Logs are also set up (i.e. Risk Log, Issue Log, Decision Log) while the Change Log is typically set up during the Planning Phase.

you.o: Still nobody's Project Manager. Present as a Project Support Office adviser on what to do next.
you.k: Knows the numbers from yesterday, plus that IT has an indicative figure near eight and a half million.
you.w: Wants the meeting to end with one named next step rather than general agreement.
you.f: Afraid Nightingale goes straight to a tender and nobody ever writes the problem down.

nightingale.o: From this meeting, Project Owner. Accountable for the project's success and for the benefits.
nightingale.k: Knows the operational pain in detail. Has heard a cost corridor, not a cost.
nightingale.w: Wants both audit findings closed and wants to be out by three o'clock.
nightingale.f: Afraid this becomes an IT project she cannot steer.

hopper.o: Initiator of the request. Business Manager from this meeting onward.
hopper.k: Knows the current process end to end. Does not yet know the delivery model.
hopper.w: Wants Nightingale to say the word own, out loud, in front of Leonardo.
hopper.f: Afraid of being made the owner of a problem she cannot fund.

leonardo.o: From this meeting, Solution Provider. Accountable for whatever gets built.
leonardo.k: Knows the LOS code base and the payment gateway's undocumented behaviour.
leonardo.w: Wants six weeks of analysis before anyone quotes a number he will be held to.
leonardo.f: Afraid a corridor figure becomes a promise the moment it is written down.

gantt.o: Project Support Office. Not yet supporting a project, because no project exists.
gantt.k: Knows where the collateral register Project-End Report is filed.
gantt.w: Wants to know whether this meeting is official, so he knows what to record.
gantt.f: Afraid decisions are being taken in rooms that produce no record.

note: Guide check: section 5.1, p.31. The Initiating Meeting is informal, usually between the project initiator and the Project Owner, plus others who could contribute to the Initiating Phase documents. Its goal is to introduce pre-project information and discuss next steps, and lessons learned from previous similar projects are a legitimate input. Its output is not a document but a shared understanding and a decision to create the Project Initiation Request. RASCI row: none, because there is not yet a project to have roles in. Approver: nobody. Page 31.
notePlain: Rule: the Initiating Meeting is informal. It is usually the person raising the idea, the Project Owner, and anyone who can help write the first documents. Its purpose is to share what is already known and agree the next step. Reports and lessons learned from earlier, similar projects can be used here. The result is not a document. It is a decision to write the Project Initiation Request. There is no RASCI row and no approver, because there is no project yet. Page 31.

title: Whose name goes at the top
where: ESM, Kirchberg — Grace Hopper's office, Lending Operations

lines.text: Monday. Sleet that cannot commit. Grace's office holds two chairs, a wall of loan files and a screen with an empty template on it.
lines.plain: It is Monday. Wet snow is falling. Grace Hopper's office has two chairs, a wall of loan files, and a screen showing an empty template.

lines.text: Three o'clock. One page. She said one page and she meant one page.
lines.plain: The deadline is 15:00. One page. Florence said one page and she meant it.

lines.text: What is it called?
lines.plain: What is the project called?

lines.text: CASTOR. Renewal of the Lending Operations System. A castor is a beaver. It builds things and it works at night. The name is provisional, and everything provisional survives forever.
lines.plain: CASTOR. The full title is Renewal of the Lending Operations System. A castor is a beaver. It builds things and it works at night. The name is temporary, and temporary names usually last for ever.

lines.text: Leonardo's estimate arrives at 09:12. Three thousand one hundred person-days. Around eight point four million all in. Twenty-six months. He has written the word indicative twice.
lines.plain: Leonardo's estimate arrives by email at 09:12. It says 3,100 person-days, about 8.4 million euro in total, and 26 months. He wrote the word indicative twice, meaning it is only a rough figure.
g: person-day
one person working for one day; the unit used to measure project effort

lines.text: Type of delivery. In-house, outsourced, mix, or not known.
lines.plain: Next box: type of delivery. The choices are in-house, outsourced, a mix of both, or not known yet.
g: type of delivery
how the work will be done: in-house, outsourced, a mix, or not yet decided

lines.text: Mix. In-house core team, outsourced platform implementation.
lines.plain: A mix. Our own core team, and an outside company to install and configure the platform.

lines.text: Florence puts her head round the door on her way to something else and does not come in.
lines.plain: Florence looks in through the door on her way somewhere else. She does not come into the room.

lines.text: Fifteenth of May 2028. Write it down.
lines.plain: The delivery date is 15 May 2028. Write that down.

lines.text: That is a need, not a promise.
lines.plain: That is what you need, not what we promise.

lines.text: Write it down.
lines.plain: Write it down anyway.

lines.text: It goes in as a target delivery date. The day it becomes a promise there will be a Charter under it.
lines.plain: I will write it in the box called target delivery date. It becomes a promise only when a Project Charter supports it.
ref: The Project Initiation Request contains basic information about the estimated effort and cost of undertaking the project as well as the timeframe for its completion and the type of delivery.

lines.text: Success criteria. Five days to one. Three days to same day. Nine months to six weeks. Two open findings to zero.
lines.plain: Now the success criteria. Paying out: from five working days to one. Reconciliation: from three days to the same day. Adding a new lending product: from nine months to six weeks. Open audit findings: from two to zero.

lines.text: Not the fourteen hundred fields?
lines.plain: Should we not also include the 1,400 re-typed fields?

lines.text: Business Case, with Ada's process map under it. High level here, or the page becomes four pages and nobody reads any of them.
lines.plain: That belongs in the Business Case, with Ada Lovelace's process map to support it. This document stays at a high level. Otherwise one page becomes four and nobody reads any of them.
g: Business Case
the document that compares options, justifies the money and recommends one solution
ref: Ensure all the relevant information is included, but at this point limit details to high-level information—finer points will be added in the form of the Business Case and other Project artefacts.

lines.text: Risks.
lines.plain: What about the risks?

lines.text: Ratification. The backstop stays a planned capability rather than a live one, so the scope can move under us.
lines.plain: The main risk is ratification. The common backstop is only planned, not yet real. So the size of the job can change while we work.

lines.text: Do not put Italy in a document that goes to the Investment Board.
lines.plain: Do not name Italy in a document that goes to the Corporate Investment Board.

lines.text: It is in the public ratification table. He can read it there, or he can read it from us.
lines.plain: The information is already public, in the official ratification table. Lorenzo can read it there, or he can read it in our document.

lines.text: Johannes Gutenberg is in the doorway holding a printout nobody asked him for.
lines.plain: Johannes Gutenberg stands in the doorway. He is holding a printed page that nobody asked him to bring.

lines.text: Before anybody signs anything. Where does this live? Version 1.0, project folder, document location filled in. Not an attachment in three mailboxes with three different dates on it.
lines.plain: Before anyone signs: where will this document be stored? Mark it version 1.0, put it in the project folder, and fill in the document location box. It must not exist as an email attachment in three mailboxes with three different dates.
ref: Manages the project documentation (versioning, archiving, etc.).

lines.text: Hello, Johannes. You did not say hello.
lines.plain: Hello, Johannes. You started talking without saying hello.

lines.text: I could accept this myself and we would be finished by lunch.
lines.plain: I could approve this document myself, and we would be finished before lunch.

lines.text: For a smaller request, yes. At eight point four million the approving authority is the Corporate Investment Board, chaired by Lorenzo de' Medici.
lines.plain: For a smaller request, yes. At 8.4 million euro the approver is the Corporate Investment Board, which Lorenzo de' Medici chairs.
g: Appropriate Governance Body
the senior committee that approves projects, agrees their objectives and releases the money
ref: Know your audience: Depending on the project size and the organisation's approval process, approval can be informal (i.e. the Project Owner (PO) accepts it), or formal (i.e. an Appropriate Governance Body (AGB) reviews and approves it).

lines.text: And it does not ask him for eight point four million. It asks him to let us spend six weeks finding out whether eight point four is the right number.
lines.plain: And the document does not ask him for 8.4 million euro. It asks him to let us spend six weeks finding out whether 8.4 million is the right figure.
ref: Depending on the project, the Project Owner (PO) or a higher-level Appropriate Governance Body (AGB) can accept the Project Initiation Request and authorise work on a more elaborate Business Case.

lines.text: Then somebody write it.
lines.plain: Then one of you write it.

choice.prompt: Florence is holding the pen out. Who writes the Project Initiation Request?
choice.promptPlain: Florence is offering the pen. Who should write the Project Initiation Request?

options.t: Grace writes it. She raised it and she is the Business Manager. I sit beside her with the template.
options.tPlain: Grace Hopper writes it. She raised the problem and she is the Business Manager. You sit next to her with the template.

reply.text: Then sit down. There are four boxes I cannot fill without you. Type of delivery, effort, approving authority, and what actually happens after they say yes.
reply.plain: Then sit down. I cannot fill in four boxes without you: type of delivery, effort, who approves it, and what happens after they agree.

options.why: Anyone can introduce a Project Initiation Request, but in many cases the Project Owner delegates its creation to the Business Manager (p.32). The RASCI row is BM Responsible, PO Accountable and Supporting, BIG Supports and is Consulted, AGB and SP Informed, PSC and PM not applicable (p.33). Sitting beside her with the template is exactly the support a Project Manager can give without taking the pen.
options.whyPlain: Anyone may raise a Project Initiation Request. In practice the Project Owner asks the Business Manager to write it (page 32). In the RASCI table the Business Manager is Responsible and the Project Owner is Accountable; the Project Manager has no letter at all (page 33). Helping with the template is support. Taking the pen is not.
ref: Note that though anyone can initiate a Project Initiation Request, in many cases the Project Owner (PO) delegates its creation to the Business Manager (BM).

options.t: I take it. I know the template and I can have a clean draft by tonight.
options.tPlain: You write it yourself. You know the template and can finish a clean draft tonight.

note: Guide check: section 5.3, pp.34-35. The Business Case captures the reasoning behind the project, its alignment with organisational strategy, the justification for the investment and the budgetary need. It must contain the justification and impact, the strategic positioning, a SWOT of several solutions with one proposed, a cost-benefit analysis per solution, synergies and interdependencies, a high-level roadmap and measurable success criteria. RASCI: AGB I, PSC C, PO A, BM R, BIG C, SP S, PM S, PCT n.a. Approver: a preliminary Project Steering Committee or a higher-level AGB, on the Project Owner's submission. It is a living document, re-examined at critical milestones, not filed away after the gate. Pages 34-35.
notePlain: Rule: the Business Case explains why the project should happen, how it fits the organisation's strategy, why the money is justified, and what the budget must be. It contains the impact, the strategic fit, a SWOT for several options with one recommended, a cost-benefit analysis for each option, links to other projects, a high-level roadmap, and success criteria that can be measured. note: Guide check: section 5.4, p.36. Approval sequence: the Business Manager consults stakeholders and helps draft; the Project Manager delivers the document; the main stakeholders review it; the Project Steering Committee accepts it; the Project Owner then sends the Business Case and Charter onward to the decision-making body for additional approval if needed, and that body accepts or rejects. notePlain: Rule: the Business Manager consults the stakeholders and helps write the Charter. The Project Manager finishes it. The main stakeholders review it. The Steering Committee accepts it. Then the Project Owner sends the Business Case and the Charter upward if a higher approval is needed. note: Guide check: section 5.5, p.37. RfP, Ready for Planning, is the first phase gate. The Project Manager assesses whether the project is ready to commence the Planning Phase and seeks approval of the Business Case and Project Charter from the Project Steering Committee. If either is not approved, the project proceeds directly to the Closing Phase for lessons learned and archiving. PM² supplies a Phase Exit Review Checklist per phase to guide that assessment alongside a review of the phase's specific goals; the Initiating sheet runs to twenty-eight questions and ends by asking whether the project is ready to proceed. RASCI: none, the checklist has no row. Approver: nobody approves the checklist itself. The Project Steering Committee authorises the phase transition it supports (p.25). Page 37.
notePlain: Rule: Ready for Planning is the first gate. The Project Manager checks whether the project is ready to start planning, and asks the Steering Committee to approve the Business Case and the Charter. If either is not approved, the project goes straight to the Closing Phase, to record lessons learned and store the documents. PM² gives one checklist per phase to guide this check, used together with a look at the goals of the phase. The Initiating sheet has 28 questions and ends by asking whether the project can move on. There is no RASCI row for the checklist and nobody approves it. The Steering Committee approves the move to the next phase. Pages 25 and 37.
